title: Pizza with extra meat and extra vegetables, thin crust

content.title: About
content.content: A thin, crispy pizza topped with tomato sauce, a generous portion of extra meat (ham, sausage, chicken) and a variety of vegetables (bell pepper, onion, mushrooms, olives). Perfect for those who love hearty and flavorful dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The thin crust is made from high‑quality wheat flour and is allowed to rest for at least 24 hours for optimal flavor.
Extra meat is usually layered to keep it juicy throughout baking.
Vegetables are finely sliced to distribute evenly across the pizza surface.
Traditionally the pizza is baked at 250 °C for 8–10 minutes.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A and potassium, supporting immunity and heart health.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The thin crust and meat deliver quick energy, useful before active activities.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The abundance of meat and cheese makes the pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight‑watching individuals.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salt in the sauce and processed meats can be high; people with hypertension should opt for a lower‑salt version.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The pizza may contain dairy, gluten, and meat ingredients that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pizza hot, cut into individual slices. Optionally garnish with fresh basil or arugula after baking for extra aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in an oven or grill to restore the crisp crust.
